scenes.heading: Cloud Service Architecture and Operations
scenes.narration: Oak & Operations. Cloud Service Architecture and Operations. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What architectural shift does AEM as a Cloud Service make?
scenes.heading: It moves from instance-centric to service-based, using n-x AEM containers driven by Cloud Manager CI/CD pipelines
scenes.body: Section 13 says AEM as a Cloud Service moves from an instance-centric model to a service-based one with n-x AEM containers driven by Cloud Manager CI/CD pipelines.

scenes.question: Why are production configuration changes outside the pipeline a problem in Cloud Service?
scenes.heading: Because configuration changes in production that bypass the pipeline break the CI/CD policy

scenes.question: What is true about indexes during a rolling deployment in Cloud Service?
scenes.heading: Old and new versions run side by side for a time, so two sets of indexes exist, and the new version is built and reindexed before the traffic switch
scenes.body: The source says rolling deployments run the old and new version side by side, so two index sets exist, and the new version's indexes are built and repositories reindexed before the traffic switch.

scenes.question: Why can checking only AEM logs miss a request in Cloud Service?
scenes.heading: Because traffic flows from the CDN to Apache and Dispatcher on Publish and then to AEM, and a request may be answered earlier in that chain
scenes.body: Section 13 says traffic flows CDN to Apache and Dispatcher to AEM, and each layer has its own log, so AEM logs alone can miss a request answered earlier in the chain.
